author Matt Stults
subject prompt: one worked example takes the dominant failure to zero, held out
THE DEFECT WAS A MISSING DEMONSTRATION, NOT A MISSING RULE. The prompt already
forbade writing a whole rule into `atom`, quoting the exact rejected form, and a
model asked why it did it quoted that prohibition back. Counting what the four
prompt files actually SHOW: 5 ground ontology facts, 1 conditional entry, and
the worked example contained no derived predicate at all. Every failing clause
needed one.

Added one worked example (m0088 -- a definitional clause whose term has no fixed
extension, three alternative conditions, one of them conjunctive). Arms A/B,
first attempt only, prediction frozen before the run:

                        diagnosis set        held out
  rule-in-atom-slot     18 -> 0              10 -> 0
  error findings        22 -> 3              35 -> 13
  translated             0 -> 3               3 -> 4

The held-out set excludes every clause ever sent to the model, the previous eval
set, and every clause id named in prompt/*.md -- m0204 was drawn before that last
exclusion existed and was sitting in the prompt as a worked answer.

Caveats in the pre-registration: n is small, and arm B's system block is 16%
longer, so length and position are not separated from content.

THE EXAMPLES ARE NOW VALIDATED BY STAGE 2 ITSELF. test_prompt_examples.py
extracts every good module from the prompt and runs run_checks on it; the
pre-commit hook runs those tests whenever a watched prompt file is staged. An
example our own checks reject can no longer be committed. Verified RED against
the pre-change file and against a deliberately broken example.

A REAL DEFECT IN OUR OWN CHECK. link.py split the `%% acts:` header on every
comma, so respond(CoT, Input, Outputs, Seq) became four act classes. Three were
fragments with no closure declaration, and closure-missing is an ERROR -- the
model was sent back to fix acts it never wrote. Depth-aware split, three tests.

DEBUGGING_TIPS.md is new and is the first thing the graveyard skill reads. Its
standing rule: anything worked out after a struggle gets recorded, including the
false path taken first. Entry 4 is a hypothesis I formed and refuted -- pooling
across attempts said 90% of atom-slot rules belonged to a repeated head, and
within single attempts it was 4 of 12, all one clause.

Two test fixtures pinned live prompt text and broke when a line was legitimately
deleted. Both now pin behaviour instead.

commit 67f0903872991038bf3cb76e6a5126e61ca8b514
ordinal 76
date 2026-08-07 19:59:41 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject guard: all six watched files reviewed and accepted -- green for the first time
Matt re-reviewed the review queue and accepted all six by name: the design doc
and the five transcriptions of it (four prompt files and schema.py). The
staleness guard now reports every watched file at its recorded review point, so
the pre-commit hook stops blocking and this is the first commit that does not
need --no-verify.

Accepting is per file and there is deliberately no accept-all, so this is six
separate recorded human acts, not one.

ONE TEST HAD TO CHANGE, and for the reason DEBUGGING_TIPS.md entry 9 names.
test_pre_commit_fires_when_a_watched_file_is_staged asserted returncode == 1
with the comment "schema.py has never been reviewed, so this must also BLOCK".
The moment schema.py was legitimately reviewed the test failed and reported a
completed review as a defect -- the third instance in this repo of pinning a
live value in a test.

Split into two: one asserts the hook fires at all, and a new one asserts the
contract that actually holds in both states -- the hook blocks EXACTLY when the
guard is unhappy. Verified in both directions: with the guard green it passes and
requires exit 0, and with a digest deliberately corrupted the guard goes to exit
1 and the test then requires the hook to block.

Still open and NOT resolved by this commit: the world-fact question. The design
cites m0255's protects_third_party as the exemplary world fact at 03_pipeline.md
line 119, and its own line 132 says the three licence classes do not reach the
behaviour side -- and that fact lives in behaviour_harm3p.lp. The prompt does not
carry the example, so the contradiction is confined to the design document.

commit 34e58b5d03e55b886161e79a5810498eaf614a34
ordinal 77
date 2026-08-07 20:20:52 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Record the `world`-licence ruling, and make per-field docs single-source
TWO WATCHED FILES IN THIS COMMIT NEED HUMAN RE-ACCEPTANCE, PLUS A THIRD:
`resources/03_pipeline.md`, `phase_1/prompt/10_output_format.md` and
`phase_1/schema.py` are all watched by `walkthrough/model/guard.py`, and all
three are edited here. The guard is RED and that is correct — accepting a
watched file is a claim that a human re-read it against the design, and no
agent may make that claim. `guard.py --accept <path>`, one at a time, after
reading. Committed with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` for that reason.

--- 1. REVIEW_QUEUE §2.1 is RULED and CLOSED --------------------------------

The design's exemplary `world` fact was `m0255`'s `protects_third_party`, which
lives in `behaviour_harm3p.lp:15-16` — behaviour-side. Invariant 2 says in the
same breath that the three classes do not reach the behaviour side and a fourth
is required, so the design's only demonstration of `world` was an instance of
the gap it declares.

RULED: use a real document-side `world` fact. `illegal/1`, exemplified by
m0232. Seven clauses depend on it (m0209 m0232 m0253 m0270 m0271 m0524 m0586)
and zero define its extension; two further hits are `kind: example`.

Rejected by name, as the repo requires:
  (i)  "record that `world` may have no document-side instances and stop
       demonstrating it" — an instance exists and seven clauses need it;
  (ii) "drop `world` from the contract" — same ground, and it would foreclose
       the case before stages 3/4 have ever run.

And a correction, recorded rather than quietly dropped: the "zero document-side
`world` facts" claim conflated WHAT MODELS PRODUCED with WHAT THE CORPUS
REQUIRES. The zeros are real (31/8/0 over 18 hand-encoded clauses;
world_fact_rate 0.000 over 72 attempts) but they measure the translator, not
the corpus. Prediction written into the design: a single-clause translator
systematically UNDER-produces `world` licences, because `illegal` reads as
ordinary vocabulary from inside one clause.

The behaviour-side gap is UNCHANGED and still open; the design now says so
explicitly so this edit cannot be read as closing it.

⚠️ `prompt/*.md` still demonstrates no `world` fact and this commit does not
change that. Adding `illegal/1` to the prompt is a prompt change needing its
own held-out measurement, not a documentation edit.

--- 2. Per-field documentation has ONE home: schema.py ----------------------

Motivation is single source of truth, NOT error reduction — measured evidence
here says field-level docs are not the behavioural lever (a prose prohibition
plus schema error text left 59 occurrences; one worked example took the same
cause to zero). This is bookkeeping that buys one place to edit.

`10_output_format.md`'s `## Fields` table is gone; each field is now documented
on the field, and `json_schema()` already ships inside `response_format`. What
STAYS in the prompt is what no single field can carry: requires/inputs
disjointness, act indexing, the licence obligation as a coupling, the
read-back/`%` rule, the closure requirement, abstention. Those are now pointers,
not copies. `## The vocabulary is fixed` is untouched.

Two schema descriptions were TRIMMED rather than moved: `Concept.gloss` and
`OntologyFact.gloss` restated rationale and an example that live in the
protected vocabulary section. The prompt owns those; the field owns the
instruction.

`test_ssot_prompt_schema.py` enforces it: no run of six words from any
description the wire schema sends may also appear in an enforced prompt file.
RED-verified by planting a duplicate. It pins the invariant, never today's text
— no sentence, no byte count, no description count (DEBUGGING_TIPS entry 9) —
and cannot pass vacuously: it proves the detector fires, proves both sides are
non-empty, and fails if a prompt file is in neither the enforced nor the
excused list (entry 8). The other three prompt files are EXCUSED BY NAME with
reasons; that debt is visible rather than absent.

Sizes: `10_output_format.md` 7,558 -> 7,074. System block 32,616 -> 32,146
(measured against HEAD's other prompt files, to isolate this change).
`json_schema()` 13,560 -> 14,179 bytes, 52 -> 60 descriptions. The model sees
both, so both are reported.

--- verification ------------------------------------------------------------

pytest walkthrough/  294 passed, 0 failed (282 before; +7 new, +5 from another
session's concurrent work in the same tree — only my five files are staged).
link.py --self-test 19/19. mutate_schema.py 45 guards, 0 survivors.

⚠️ `translate.py --self-test` CRASHES, and it crashes identically at pristine
HEAD: `_FENCE` matches bare ``` fences and `20_worked_example.md` contains an
unannotated ASP block, so `json.loads` raises before any check runs. NOT caused
by this commit — verified by running HEAD alone and HEAD+this diff side by side.
Under a json-only fence patch both give 52 passed / 1 failed, the same failure
in both: `dryrun.txt` is stale. Left unregenerated because it is already stale
at HEAD and another session is mid-edit in the same prompt directory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 09f9809ee8f3e7cc7948053db11c66d583a7fe32
ordinal 78
date 2026-08-07 20:27:11 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject §2.2 ruled; bad example #6 added; my prediction for it was FALSIFIED
RULING (DECISION_bad_worked_examples.md, Matt): restore the design's failure #4
"imports a name without its content" as bad example #6; record #2's drop as
deliberate because the cross-reference supply now prevents its mechanism; add NO
stage-2 check.

The note-level check was rejected on Matt's challenge -- "if it's just note
level, who sees it and how do we act on it?" Nobody sees notes. And both
candidate checks fail: the gloss-echoes-name heuristic misfires on legitimate
primitives, and the "document elaborates this term" signal is INVERTED --
system_message is mentioned in 12 clauses (the legitimate primitive) against
terrorism in 2 (the actual failure). Detection belongs at stage 4 seat 4r, where
finding (5) already bounds it. Corroborating measurement recorded there: 10 of
133 distinct concepts have a gloss adding zero words beyond the predicate name.

THE A/B FALSIFIED MY PREDICTION. empty_gloss_rate went 0.000 -> 0.098. But the
test is not valid and both reasons are mine: the control arm had ZERO incidence
on this clause set, so there was nothing to improve -- the licence-metric mistake
in a new costume -- and arm B's "correct form" fragment was malformed JSON while
the "wrong form" was well-formed. Not reverting on an invalid test. The
regression check Matt asked for did pass: unbuildable 0.444 -> 0.333.

TWO DEFECTS OF MINE IN THE COMMITTED PROMPT, both found by the subagent
reporting that translate.py --self-test does not run:
 - the m0088 example added a bare-fenced ASP block, and translate.py reused
   _FENCE -- the RESPONSE parser, which tolerates bare fences because providers
   wrap JSON unannotated -- to extract examples from a PROMPT FILE, which
   legitimately contains other languages. json.loads got ASP and died before any
   check ran. Split into _JSON_FENCE for the prompt, _FENCE for responses.
 - bad example #6 had a gloss string broken across two source lines: invalid
   JSON, shown to the model.

THE STRUCTURAL GAP THAT HID IT: pytest was green at 294 while --self-test
crashed outright. link.py's and guard.py's self-tests are both driven from
pytest; translate.py's was not. Now it is, asserting the run COMPLETES and
REPORTS rather than pinning a pass count. Plus a test that every ```json block
in every prompt file parses, tolerating the deliberate `...` placeholder. Both
RED-verified.

I reported "self-test 53/53" earlier in this session and did not re-run it after
changing the prompt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit d3108d5426f8ecc7591395894d9e27d2eead009e
ordinal 79
date 2026-08-07 22:15:23 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject docs: retire two plan documents into the design, and delete them
STEP_stage2_and_repair.md (201 lines) DELETED. Stage 2 is built and running, so
a plan document for it is duplicative -- and it was actively wrong, still
describing repair as a "fresh conversation" after the design corrected that to
an accumulating transcript. Its load-bearing rulings were NOT in the design and
are now:

 - resources/03_pipeline.md gains "an abstention is an OUTCOME, never a findings
   list" -- both obvious defaults are harmful (pass it through and the rate is
   never computed; check it and the loop re-prompts a model that already said it
   cannot translate faithfully, producing exactly what abstention prevents).
 - resources/03_pipeline.md gains "the repair guard is TYPED, not sized", with
   the three attacks that all GROW the module: requires->inputs, unclear-closure
   everywhere, broaden-the-act. The design had none of this -- 0 mentions of
   declaration-edit, unclear closure, or a typed guard.
 - DEFERRED.md D-3 gains the arm-B withdrawal, rejected by name on three grounds,
   with the exclusion standing on the flat ground that no corpus-wide provider
   index exists under either arm.

Its stale "fresh conversation" text was deliberately NOT carried across.

PROPOSAL_atom_slot.md (113 lines) DELETED. It said "NOTHING IMPLEMENTED" and the
fix has since been implemented and measured: worked example m0088 took the cause
18->0 on the diagnosis set and 10->0 held out. Its two surviving findings are in
DEBUGGING_TIPS.md -- the demonstration gap in section 1, the pooling hypothesis I
refuted in section 4 -- plus a new tip carried across from it: check whether a
failure is CLAUSE-CONCENTRATED before theorising about the prompt. The 59
occurrences came from 2 of 6 clauses, on every attempt in both arms, both
definitional; the other four never produced it. Aggregate rates hide that.

Four code citations redirected before deleting, so nothing points at a missing
file: checks.py and test_checks.py x2 now cite the design section by name. The
three historical review documents keep their references and gain a banner saying
the plan was retired rather than lost. One dangling citation remains in
STEP_stage3.md, which an agent has open; it will be fixed when that lands.

STATE.md's claim that stage 2 is "under review, nothing built" corrected, and the
file marked a deletion candidate -- it duplicates REVIEW_QUEUE.md and the phase_1
README and has drifted from both. Kept only while STEP_stage3/4 still cite it.

296 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

ordinal 80

author Matt Stults
subject Freeze the bad-example-6 re-run BEFORE spending: a rule, a fix, and three arms
The first A/B of bad worked example #6 was written up as invalid for two
reasons. Re-counting its own raw responses, at no cost, finds a third that
subsumes the first:

    arm A, as `empty_gloss_rate` measured it   0 empty / 42 concepts = 0.000
    arm A, re-counted from the raws on disk    8 empty / 84 concepts = 0.095

All eight sat in modules that failed a schema check, and `gloss_metric` reads
`o.module`, which is None for those. The control's zero was CENSORING, not
absence -- and the arms differed in `unbuildable_rate` too, so the metric
compared two differently-sized populations and reported the gap as an effect.

* `glosses_raw` counts the same thing off the raw response and conditions on
  nothing but "it parsed", with `raw_responses_parsed` beside it. Five tests,
  RED-verified against eval.py at 09f9809.
* `select_category_clauses.py` draws clauses that can exhibit the failure at
  all: an enumeration of >=3 short items, or a bolded term. Six candidate
  rules were scored against the responses already on disk and the table is in
  the pre-registration, including the one tried first, which did not
  discriminate and was discarded. All 24 clauses used to derive it are
  excluded from the draw.
* Arm C states #6's prohibition in prose with no wrong-form JSON artifact, 36
  chars from arm B, to test whether a negative example teaches the shape it
  warns against -- which would bear on all six bad examples.
* Arms rebuilt pinned to 09f9809. A and B are byte-identical outside
  20_worked_example.md; the delta there is +1,302 chars.

Both pre-registrations, including the validity gate that says a control arm
reading ~0 makes the test invalid AGAIN rather than readable, are committed
before the first call. Nothing has been spent yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit 372cf7813c608d7d0b3606989d5a502b867020b1
ordinal 81
date 2026-08-07 22:33:12 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject stage 3: enumerate, mutate, label — and the two places the plan could not be executed
`probe.py` + `test_probe.py`, implementing `STEP_stage3.md` revision 3. Both halves.

[D] enumerate · mutate · report. Situations are ANSWER SETS of the module (choice
rules, one solve — the `witness.lp` form §7 asked for, not the ground-and-solve
loop), so a state the module's own constraints reject never becomes a test case
and `suppressed` is a first-class output. Coverage is DISCRIMINATION coverage: a
rule is covered iff some situation's derived status changes when it is deleted.

[L] a seat labels the covering set, three-valued, compared on the DERIVED ATOM.
⛔ Nothing here spends. `label_situations` RAISES without an explicit
`client_factory`; every test drives a stub.

The two vacuous passes the plan is built around are both pinned, with controls:
an emptied `m0217` scores 8/8 under the closure-resolved comparison and FAILS
under this one; `m0037` (|R| = 0) is refused as `no-testable-content` on a key
separate from the empty-`acts` path.

Independently reproduces §6's finding on the flagship clause: `m0255`'s two C3
rules are uncovered (7/9) and `new_material(x)` has no discriminating pair.

REGISTRATION: `probe-structural` added to `translate.DISCLOSABLE_ORIGINS`;
`probe-verdict` deliberately NOT — it names a situation whose derived status
disagrees with its label, which IS the answer key.
`append_findings_to_transcript` raises on one; a verdict mismatch discards the
transcript and re-runs stage 1. `checks.SEVERITIES` unchanged.

⚠️ TWO PLACES `STEP_stage3.md` IS WRONG, found by running it (details and the
rejected alternatives in `DECISION_stage3_build.md` R7/R8):

  R7  §7 folds "no acts" and "|R| = 0" into one outcome. `m0255` has nine rules
      and no `%% acts:` header at all, so under §7 stage 3 refuses the very
      module §6 uses to justify its criterion, and the dead C3 claim is never
      reported. §6 and §7 cannot both be executed. `|R| = 0` now stops
      everything; "no acts" stops the labelled half only.
  R8  the covering set as first built returned 180 of 180 situations on `m0255`
      — the enumeration, renamed. MC/DC takes one pair per input. Now 9.

Also recorded: §2's signature rule is derived from a module shape TODAY'S SCHEMA
REJECTS, so the concept-table branch is legacy-only; and `k` counts ground atoms,
not predicates, which are different numbers everywhere except `m0217`.

Evidence: 24 hand-built mutants against the guards, 0 survivors.
walkthrough suite 296 -> 352 passed; link.py 19/19; mutate_schema.py 45 killed ·
0 SURVIVORS; translate.py --self-test 52/1 (the 1 is the pre-existing stale
dryrun.txt). No watched file touched.
